Both define `layout.preflight` with different routes: COMMAND-SURFACE has typed(..., "LayoutEditor::preflight") Surface::Viewer -> Viewer::run_command -> editor.preflight_json(); this lane has entry(..., "viewer.layout_preflight") -> Viewer::layout_preflight -> report_json. Keeping both rows fails `command ids are unique` (action_records) and ui_seed refuses the whole catalog (duplicate author id studio.command.layout-preflight). After the merge, this lane's rows built with entry() get Surface::Run, so COMMAND-SURFACE's action_records filter (surface == Run) puts "viewer.layout_open" etc. into corpus_methods and the `stale` assert fails. COMMAND-SURFACE's p() sets required:true, so corpus_json reports every layout.export_pdf parameter as required while DRIVE_VIEWER says may. viewer_domain() maps unknown methods to "vector", so the five new DRIVE_VIEWER rows get canonical ids vector.layout_open, vector.export_layout_pdf, ... in help and ui_seed.

findings.what: host_loss `paragraph_break_inside_paragraph_not_drawn` is false. The break IS drawn. The pieces are joined with their clusters at story offsets, and reflow_flow -> layout paragraph.rs build_items runs UAX #14 on the story text: the LF between the two glyph clusters is a Mandatory opportunity (opp_after), so a forced penalty ends the line there. Repeated terminators also make blank lines (blank_lines). What is actually lost is the paragraph boundary: the text after the break keeps the first paragraph's style, space before and after, and first-line indent. No text vanishes: every visible byte is in exactly one piece, and the spans are clipped into that piece. The test asserts only that the code is reported and that glyphs_drawn > 0, and the 20 pt frame overflows after one line, so it does not prove that the text on both sides of the break is drawn.
findings.scenario: ReplaceText "ab\ncd" into a tall frame: the PDF shows two lines, but the receipt says the break was not drawn.
findings.fix: Rename to `paragraph_break_inside_paragraph_set_as_line_break` (element stories, count) and fix the manual line to match. Optionally give the test a tall frame and assert page_texts(...)[0] holds both sides.

findings.what: With pdfx.x4_2010 and a CMYK or gray output intent (the test uses the CMYK ICC), story text with no style fill is painted DeviceRGB black. PDF/X-4 does not allow device RGB unless the output intent is RGB. press check_pdfx4 has no colour-space rule (pdfx.rs:192-249), so self_check.all_passed can be true, while the written file carries GTS_PDFXVersion PDF/X-4. receipt.conformance does stay not_proven: ignore_preflight cannot change it, and there is no other path that changes it.
findings.scenario: The test pdfx4_with_a_cmyk_output_intent... writes an X-4-identified file with DeviceRGB text against a CMYK intent.
findings.fix: Set default_fill from the intent: components 4 -> Colour::DeviceCmyk([0,0,0,1]), 1 -> DeviceGray(0.0), otherwise DeviceRgb. When pdfx is X4 and the self-check fails (!all_passed), refuse `pdfx_self_check_failed` before write_atomic (the bytes are already in hand at :674). Style fills that are RGB under a non-RGB intent stay engine losses.
